newsitem.title: INDIA: India's MRPL to issue convertible bonds.
newsitem.headline: India's MRPL to issue convertible bonds.

text.p: Indian refiner Mangalore Refineries and Petrochemicals Ltd (MRPL) said on Wednesday it planned to issue fully convertible debentures to its promoters to raise 7.26 billion rupees.
"It is proposed to part finance the expansion cost interalia by issue of fully convertible debentures (FCDs) to the extent of 7.26 billion rupees," it said in a note to shareholders.
The company plans to raise the refining capacity at its Mangalore facility to nine million tonnes of crude oil a year from the current three million tonnes.
MRPL said the expansion cost has been estimated at 36.9 billion rupees by the Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India.
FCDs worth 3.63 billion rupees each will be issued to Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd and Indian Rayon and Industries Ltd and its associates, it said.
The terms of conversion of FCDs into equity shares will be determined in accordance with the prevailing guidelines, it said.
"As a result of conversion of the FCDs, the holding of lthe two promoting groups will increase to approximately 37.35 percent each (from 26 percent each now)," MRPL said.
The company has called for an extraordinary general meeting at Mangalore on June 27 to seek shareholders' approval.
